title: Reassess corrections within one whole change review gate
goal: Establish whether the complete current delivered scope is acceptable after owned corrections.
context: Implementation is complete; a prior attempt at the same whole-change gate may have requested changes.
trigger: The author submits the complete candidate or its corrected successor for independent assessment.
preconditions: The requested scope and relevant project authority are identifiable.

interaction.action: Provides the complete delivered scope, governing requirements/design/delivery basis and relevant evidence, identifying corrections since any earlier attempt.
Assesses the full claim scope, examines changed subjects and affected interactions, and determines what prior support remains applicable.
Records the current judgment, exact subjects, findings and rationale while preserving earlier attempts.
Reports whether the current whole-change judgment can support the separate Verify stage.

expected_outcome: An adequate independent judgment covers the complete current Change through one gate, with honest attempt history and no milestone approval substitution.

alternatives.outcome: It receives one whole-change gate without a preceding duplicate milestone review.

alternatives.condition: The correction is narrow and prior support demonstrably remains applicable.
alternatives.outcome: Reassessment reuses justified support without mechanically rereading unchanged files or rerunning unaffected checks.

failures.condition: Impact is broad or uncertain, or material findings remain.
failures.outcome: The reviewer expands assessment or withholds approval; a narrow rereview cannot imply adequate whole-change coverage.

failures.condition: Implementation changed after an approval without renewed applicability assessment.
failures.outcome: The old approval does not automatically cover the new candidate.

sources.basis: User-selected requirement-first workflow and one mandatory whole-change Code Review gate. Proposed requirement analysis only; existing product contracts remain active until coordinated adoption. No new Function, AR, implementation or approval is inferred.

Document-based author assessment under the explicit Constitution exception confirms this Scenario as requirement-analysis knowledge. It is not independent review, executed product evidence or workflow activation.
